newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares soar to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares soar to higher close.

text.p: Bullish Chilean stocks closed broadly higher again Wednesday on demand for electrical and retail stocks and on fresh rumors of a cut in interest rates, brokers said.

The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares bucked the trend on Wall Street and ended 0.71 percent higher at 127.16 points. The all-share IGPA ended 0.72 percent up at 5561.65 points on booming volume of 28 billion pesos.

Electrical shares continued their run-up, with power generators showing the biggest gains on market perceptions that a drought in central Chile is over and that share prices in the power sector had fallen too much.
Endesa closed 2.3 percent higher at 291.50 pesos, and Colbun rose 4.7 percent to 44 pesos.
"Endesa is sort of setting the tone for the market," said a broker. "It took too much punishment because of the worries about the drought."
Both Endesa and Colbun have big investments in the hydroelectric sector and were among the most vulnerable to drought.
Endesa's parent company Enersis was also higher, closing 0.3 percent up at 273 pesos.

Shares in the retail sector were mostly higher, with Santa Isabel up 2.6 percent to 760 pesos, still on the back of its sale of 36 percent of total equity to the Velox group of Argentina, brokers said. Also, Flemings Research upgraded Santa Isabel from hold to buy, citing the purchase by Velox, which owns the Disco supermarket chain.
Retailer Almacenes Paris was also up, closing 2.3 percent higher at 430 pesos.

Pharmaceuticals maker Laboratorio Chile closed one percent higher at 490 pesos and was the day's heaviest volume issue, following its auction of 24.7 million shares at between 482.50 and 483 pesos apiece for a total of about $28.5 million.
Rumors that the Central Bank might cut interest rates by a quarter or a half a percentage point sooner than mid-June or July, as originally expected, reinforced the bullish mood, brokers said.

Expectations of a rate cut have been fuelled by official figures showing lackadaisical growth so far this year, especially last week's Central Bank report showing relatively tepid 3.9 percent growth in the first quarter.
Decliners included Telecom de Chile A series, off 1.6 percent to 3,335 pesos, and CB Capital of the Cruz Blanca group, off 3.3 percent to 14.5 pesos.
Thursday is a holiday in Chile to observe Corpus Christi. Government offices, markets and most businesses are closed. Activity will return to normal on Friday.
